<!-- Maintainer template. Maintainers remove the "needs approval" label when opening their own work items. If you are not a maintainer, use "Feature request" instead. -->

### Problem

Who hits this, when it happens, and what it costs them. Written so someone outside the conversation can tell whether they have the problem.

### Outcome

What is true for the user after this ships. Their situation, not our work.

### Scope

In:

Out:

The out list should not be empty. What this issue is not doing is the part that keeps it finishable.

### Success criteria

How anyone decides it worked, checkable by a person who did not write this issue.

- at least one criterion says how it is measured, and against what baseline
- at least one says what must not regress

### Open questions

Every choice that is still undecided, with what would answer it and who decides. If you wrote "probably", "maybe" or "we should just" anywhere above, it belongs here instead.

### Constraints (optional)

Only what genuinely cannot change, each with its reason or its source. "Has to keep working on the self-hosted path" is a constraint. "Do it in service X" is a design decision, and that one belongs to whoever builds it.

### Evidence

Links to the call, query, thread or customer message behind this. Link them instead of restating their numbers, because a number copied into an issue rots while the issue stays open.

---

For whoever picks this up: the approach is yours to choose. Anything under "Open questions" is to be resolved with the author before it is built, not decided silently in code.
